act_title: Transfer of Property Act, 1882 (Act No. 4 of 1882) - Leases of Immovable Property
authority: Parliament of India / Ministry of Law and Justice

sources.title: Lease Defined
sources.summary: A lease of immovable property is a transfer of a right to enjoy such property, made for a certain time, express or implied, or in perpetuity, in consideration of a price paid or promised, or of money, a share of crops, service or any other thing of value.

sources.title: Duration of Certain Leases in Absence of Written Contract or Local Usage
sources.summary: In the absence of a contract or local law to the contrary, a lease of immovable property for agricultural or manufacturing purposes is deemed to be from year to year, terminable by six months' notice; and a lease for any other purpose is deemed to be from month to month, terminable by fifteen days' notice expiring with the end of a month of tenancy.

sources.title: Rights and Liabilities of Lessor and Lessee
sources.summary: The lessor is bound to disclose material defects in the property. The lessor shall be deemed to contract that if the lessee pays the rent and performs the contract, the lessee may hold the property during the time without interruption (quiet enjoyment).

sources.title: Determination of Lease (How Leases End)
sources.summary: A lease of immovable property determines by lapse of time, by the happening of an event specified in the agreement, by express or implied surrender, or by forfeiture for breach of an express condition.
